The horrifying human zoos: Shocking images show how 'primitive' tribesmen were caged alongside animals to be gawped at by Westerners

Caged in enclosures in Madrid's Retiro Park, they were described as 'strange', 'disfigured', 'brutal' and 'subhuman'.  It was in the spring of 1887 that Spain's Queen Maria Cristina inaugurated the Exhibition of the Philippines, and over the course of six months, thousands flocked down to the iconic location to observe natives from the Igorot tribe. They had been shipped from the Philippines, then a Spanish colony, and were put on display as part of a practice that stripped them of their dignity and reduced them to curiosities for the entertainment of the public.
